Strapped some camera gear on the bike and went out to shoot a rodeo last week end, pure personal interest, $0 potential commercial value. A couple of shots posted here and here.

Some time ago a friend of mine who is an airbrush artist and I visited the National Gallery and wandered through a contemporary art exhibit. I get the theory behind displaying rakes and shovels on the wall, boxes of cornflakes stacked in the corner, and a pristine toilet in the middle of the floor - everyday items can be art, and I do get that - however the exhibit seemed a little much and the idea of taking it a step into the absurd has been drifting around in my mind ever since. The other day I happened to be in a second hand store and saw a nice scuffed up (white) wooden frame holding a sad and unkept pastel landscape painting that I bought it for $6.99 - I took the pastel landscape out and will be starting a series of images of everyday items that I come across inside that frame, with an eye to the absurd.

A side project using the frame came to mind when my 8 year old grandson saw it, held it up to his face, and asked me to take a picture of him pretending to be a picture - he wants it in black and white. There are a few things to work out but I think it will be a fun project.

Both of the above projects have potential commercial value however as with all things of this nature, time will tell.

On the books is a visit to document what was described to me as "an abandoned pioneer era graveyard" about 100km away. I imagine that it is pretty well overgrown and will be waiting until later in the fall when the grass, shrubs, etc... are dying - both so I can see the headstones through the foliage better as well as to add a little atmosphere. It will be an early evening shoot.

Of course there is also my ongoing project of winning the lottery so that I don't need my current day job and can spend most of my time with a camera :-)

Silly projects sometimes grow teeth. http://blog.lpvshow.com/post/123690402315/the-brick-by-noel-camardo-discussed-in-episode is a good podcast (if you're into photography/photobooks). I can talk shit about contemporary art one day, one installation, and absolutely love it the next. "Dude is just photographing a brick on his garage from his window" - yeah, but...suddenly, for ME it starts to work.
